newsitem.title: PERU: Peru's Fujimori says he wants more hostage talks.
newsitem.headline: Peru's Fujimori says he wants more hostage talks.

text.p: President Alberto Fujimori told a three-man guarantors' commission on Friday that he would continue efforts to resolve Peru's 80-day-old hostage crisis peacefully, a member of the commission said.

The announcement by Archbishop Juan Luis Cipriani defused tension and renewed optimism that talks for a peaceful solution to the hostage standoff at the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima could resume.
Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) rebels holding 72 hostgaes in the residence had charged that the government planned to overrun the besieged residence by force and broke off talks.
Cipriani noted that Fujimori and Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto agreed at a meeting in Canada last month to seek a peaceful solution to the crisis and prevent loss of life.
"We have received the express confirmation of the president of this very same intention from the president of the republic in a meeting...today," Cipriani said in a statement read to reporters.
